bootstrap.intro: First, set up the database. Then you'll choose whether to start a new world or join an existing mesh — and, if you're starting fresh, create your operator account.
bootstrap.schema_fresh: Fresh database — the complete schema installs in one step.
join_host.already_connected: Already connected to a host — this resumes the sync where it left off (no host URL needed).
join_host.approval_body: On the host box: sign in to its operator plane, open {link} → Host adoption console → Pending adoption requests → Approve. Then come back here and re-submit — the sync begins.
join_host.approval_title: Request sent — the host operator must approve it.
join_host.discover_help: Checks the public front door, and — if you opt in — scans your own local network. No address needed.
join_host.heading: Join an existing mesh
join_host.intro: Connect this node to a federation already in play. It syncs the whole game — map foundation, constitution, and institutions — and becomes a read-only mirror. There's no institution-building: you're playing the same game as the rest of the mesh.
join_host.join_key_optional: (optional — leave blank to request the host operator's approval)
join_host.mesh_id_label: This node's mesh id (give it to the host)
join_host.none_found: No federations found. Enter a host URL manually below, or check your network range and try again.
join_host.syncing_body: Connected — pulling the corpus in the background. Live progress is shown below; this finishes on its own (and resumes if interrupted). You can leave this page.
mode_fork.footer: This choice is one-way for the life of the instance. Tearing down and starting over is docker compose down -v.
mode_fork.heading: How should this node join the game?
mode_fork.intro: Your operator account is set up. Every node in a mesh plays the same game — so the only question is whether this node starts a world or joins one that already exists.
mode_fork.join_body: Connect to a host already in the federation. Everything syncs in — the map foundation, the constitution, and every institution — and this node becomes a read-only mirror. No institution-building; you're playing the same game as the rest of the mesh.
mode_fork.solo_body: Build the game here — author the constitution, load the map, draw districts, seat the institutions. You become the canonical game, and other nodes federate to you. Recommended for the first node in a federation.
operator_setup.account_claimed: Account claimed. Linking a mesh identity by device key lives on the Identity page.
operator_setup.channels_intro: The channels beneath the role cards — turn any on individually, and finish the infrastructure config where a channel needs it.
operator_setup.channels_locked: Roles become available once the operator account above is created.
operator_setup.err_create_founder: Could not create the operator account.
operator_setup.err_roles: Could not turn on the roles.
operator_setup.full_console: Prefer the full console? Open the operator console →
operator_setup.heading: Set up your node
operator_setup.intro: Five steps: claim your account, name the instance, pick a role, finish its setup, and you're set. You're the founding operator, so every role is yours to switch on directly.
operator_setup.localhost_warning: — localhost only works on this computer; use your LAN/public address for real peers.
operator_setup.needs_setup_note: Infrastructure config comes next — you can turn a role on now and finish its setup there.
operator_setup.needs_setup_title: Some roles still need setup before they work:
operator_setup.path_a: Path A — a fresh local account. Your physical-operator credentials; the password works on this box only.
operator_setup.path_b_body: Already an operator elsewhere on the mesh? You can recognise yourself across boxes by device-key possession — a key your identity already trusts signs a one-time proof; no password is ever replayed between boxes. On this box: claim the account above first, then link the mesh identity from Identity → devices — only the Ed25519 public key enrols; the secret never leaves your device.
operator_setup.path_b_title: Path B — link an existing mesh identity
operator_setup.reach_open_body: Set the address peers dial to reach this box.
operator_setup.reach_question: Who should be able to reach this node?
operator_setup.reach_solo_body: Runs on this computer. No address needed — you can open it to others later when you're ready to accept peers.
operator_setup.restart_required: The address changed. Re-run the start command (docker compose up -d) so the containers pick it up before peers join.
operator_setup.role_archivist_consent: Governed — at founding you self-assert; later changes go through shared consent.
operator_setup.role_archivist_duty: Serve the app itself — uptime and bandwidth for real people.
operator_setup.role_archivist_what: A full peer serving browser players the whole application.
operator_setup.role_identity_broker_cons: Governed — the heaviest bar: co-affected peers consent to later changes.
operator_setup.role_identity_broker_duty: Hold a sealed DNS token; grant names and certs to peers.
operator_setup.role_identity_broker_what: Real names and certificates for mesh nodes — the heaviest duty.
operator_setup.role_intro: A role is a friendly grouping over the capability channels — no new power. Roles are infrastructure duties, not citizen privilege (they buy no vote or seat). As the founding operator you self-assert directly; once a government seats, governed roles return to shared consent for later changes.
operator_setup.role_record_keeper_consen: Self-asserted — one click. Your own infrastructure choice.
operator_setup.role_record_keeper_duty: Keep your box on and synced; serve the shared record to peers.
operator_setup.role_record_keeper_what: Mirror the public record and keep the world's geodata flowing.
operator_setup.role_social_moderator_con: Governed — at founding you self-assert; later changes go through shared consent.
operator_setup.role_social_moderator_dut: Run the homeserver and media plumbing the commons ride on.
operator_setup.role_social_moderator_wha: Host the live rooms — chat, voice, and the surfaces they run on.
operator_setup.share_intro: Hand a colleague a one-file start script. Solo = they found their own world; Join = they mirror this one (needs your node address set above).
operator_setup.share_join_warning: Set a reachable node address above first, or the join script won't know where to dial.
setup_exportbackuppanel.build_a_portable: Build a portable .tar.gz snapshot of this instance — every table that's part of the FK-downstream graph of jurisdictions, plus settings and rasters. Restoring this bundle on another instance via Step 0's Restore from a backup panel reproduces the full state, including district maps. Runs async via Horizon; large exports (full rasters) take 20–40 minutes.
setup_importbackuppanel.already_have_a_t: Already have a .tar.gz exported from another instance? Upload it here to skip ahead. The backend validates the manifest's schema version before restoring — older snapshots are refused with a clear message. After a successful restore you'll land on whichever wizard step matches the bundle's saved progress (so a backup taken at Step 3 drops you back at Step 3).
setup_importbackuppanel.only_tables_actu: Only tables actually present in the uploaded bundle get restored — un-selected tables on this instance are left alone.
setup_importbackuppanel.upload_complete_: Upload complete — restoring database (pg_restore). May take several minutes on a full-rasters bundle.

step0_cosmic_address.intro: This is the Cosmopolitan Governance App — a federated, open-source platform implementing A Fair Constitution. It models every institution the Template defines (residency, elections, legislatures, executives, judiciaries, organizations) as interactive, automatable software, from neighborhood scale up to planetary scale and beyond.

Every constitutional and economic default here seeds each jurisdiction's own amendable settings and cascades to new child jurisdictions as they come online — so they don't reinvent the wheel. Each jurisdiction can still amend its own values locally once its legitimacy gate activates. The game mode below is a world-wide property, not per-jurisdiction.

You can depart from them here. After setup, any further amendments must go through valid legislative acts.

Open the jurisdiction viewer to inspect boundaries, populations, raster overlays, dual-footprint relationships, and the map health checks — then accept the map data there (planet scope). step2_map_data.tooltip_p2: The rest describe the world: disputed borders that must coexist in one game space, island groups administered from a distant mainland, a national source that records the same village at two levels, a country the population raster doesn't cover. Accepting is frequently the correct resolution.
step2_map_data.tooltip_p3: A large count is normal on a full-planet import. What matters is whether the structural check is clear — open the viewer and read each check's own explainer.

step3_districts.rewind_confirm:
Rewind mapping to the start?

This DELETES every autoscale-generated district map and re-mints fresh founding drafts. Sizing, the founding boards, and the precomputed adjacency are kept; adopted/operator maps are never touched. The run stays halted — press Resume when ready.
step3_districts.rewind_title: Delete generated maps and re-mint fresh founding drafts (sizing + precompute kept)
step3_districts.sizing_pass: Sizing pass — parent legislatures (re-verifies every parent)
step3_districts.tip_a_compactness: Measures whether the district's outer boundary is compact or irregular using the Convex Hull Ratio: district area divided by the area of its convex hull (1.0 = perfectly convex).
step3_districts.tip_a_constituentless: Jurisdictions with no constituents. Within the seat band such a jurisdiction is one at-large district; above the ceiling it is line-split by the leaf ladder, whose rungs are tried in order (shortest split-line, box, community cells, vertical strips, horizontal strips, whole components) until one files. The rows name the rung that filed each map; "unrecorded" maps were drawn before the ladder timings were kept.
step3_districts.tip_a_contiguity: Contiguity is considered broken only when it was achievable in the first place. Geographic impossibilities are exempt. These include island jurisdictions with no land border to any sibling, members completely surrounded by jurisdictions too large to combine without breaching the constitutional ceiling, and single-member districts, which are never constitutionally incongruous.
step3_districts.tip_a_diversity: For every composite scope, the drawn district seat counts are compared with the Optimal the map view shows: the balanced partition of the scope's composed seats with the lowest average Droop threshold (the most uniform political diversity), a lawful one-jurisdiction single counted beside it. Optimal means the two match; Not optimal means the drawing differs, which includes every recorded floor exception.
step3_districts.tip_a_equality: Measures how evenly each district's population-per-seat matches the ideal "one person, one vote" standard. Lower deviation means each vote carries more equal weight. Includes every composite district on the planet; at-large single districts have no deviation by construction.
step3_districts.tip_a_integrity: Judged on the composite maps only (jurisdictions with constituents). Districts drawn along pre-existing administrative boundaries keep communities intact; a line-split piece appears inside a composite map only where a constituent holds more seats than the ceiling allows and has no subdivisions of its own. Leaf maps have their own section below.
step3_districts.tip_a_legality: Every district map must seat exactly its apportioned total (no drift), keep every district inside the 5–9 seat band, and record any floor exception (Art. II §2) or ceiling exception (a forced 1- or 0-seat landing lifted to 2 with bonus seats) where the geography forces one.
step3_districts.tip_b_contiguity: A panel is contiguous when its constituent jurisdictions form one connected piece of the chamber's border graph. A break is forced when the panel spans islands or separate landmasses that touch no sibling. The remaining breaks are the price of the even split: Clumping Spread comes before Contiguity, so where no contiguous even split exists a constituent joins the nearest panel by centroid.
step3_districts.tip_b_diversity: Tracks whether the clumps hold an even number of constituent parts. With equal seats per panel, equal member counts give equal representation. Spread is the difference between the largest and smallest panel of a map: 0 means every panel holds the same count, 1 means "equal except one", anything over 1 is uneven.
step3_districts.tip_b_legality: A panel map may never seat more than the Type B ceiling (the Type A total, capped so seats never exceed people), must place every constituent jurisdiction in exactly one panel, must hold no empty panel, and its panel seats must add up to the chamber's Type B seats. A chamber whose ladder already fits keeps one panel per constituent; a chamber whose ceiling holds less than one panel lawfully seats none.

step4_scale_up.intro: Every legislature receives its institutions. The shell set lands first in set-based batches: executive, court, election board, public square and halls, public treasury. Then one lane per legislature schedules its founding election and its races, and files the committees and departments as system acts. Halt, resume and roll back at any time. Continue locks the result.

step5_simulate.heading: Simulate
step5_simulate.intro: Step 4 built the institutions. Step 5 populates them: residents decided per place, people minted, the founding elections fielded and counted by the real engine, representatives seated, chambers grown, courts seated, and civic life modelled. Each stage runs the constitution's own forms, never a shortcut. Halt, resume and roll back at any time. Continue locks the result.
step5_simulate.lock_title_pending: Run the acceptance scan before locking
step5_simulate.lock_title_ready: Lock the simulated world and continue
step5_simulate.lock_title_review: Resolve the unresolved scopes, or finish with documented exclusions
step5_simulate.lock_title_wait: Continue opens when the run is verified
step5_simulate.notice_halt: Halt requested. Lanes stop at their next claim boundary; resume picks up where it stopped.
step5_simulate.notice_resumed: Resumed. The pump re-seeds workers within the minute.
step5_simulate.notice_resuming: Resuming the unfinished run — re-enumerating cleanly.
step5_simulate.notice_started: Run started. The work-list enumerates first; lanes follow within the minute.
step5_simulate.readiness_not_done: the run must finish before verification
step5_simulate.readiness_pending: verification pending — run the acceptance scan before locking

step5_simulate.rollback_confirm:
Roll back this SIMULATION run: clear its work-list and lanes so a fresh run can re-enumerate. The world it already produced (cohorts, people, seats, civic records) is LEFT IN PLACE, and Step 4's institutions and every map are untouched.

The run must be halted or done. Continue?
step5_simulate.scope_sub: · pick what to simulate — prerequisites are pulled in automatically, so nothing a chosen aspect needs can be left out. People and wallets always run.
step5_simulate.timing_note: The bar is each part's share of total lane-seconds. Watch Between claims: a lane that sits idle is a lane not working. Compare a stage's avg before and after a change to prove it faster or slower.
step5_simulate.timing_sub: where the time goes · avg per part, total across all lanes
step5_simulate.verify_pending_note: The run finished but the acceptance scan never ran. It is bounded and resumable — run the verify phase, then lock. This state cannot be forced past.

step6_confirm.finish_heading: What happens when you click Finish
step6_confirm.finish_point_1: The confirmation and the data-quality snapshot are recorded on the instance settings.
step6_confirm.finish_point_2: setup_completed_at is stamped. /setup redirects home from then on.
step6_confirm.finish_point_3: Nothing else runs. Institutions were Step 4's; the simulation is Step 5's.
step6_confirm.heading: Confirm & Close
step6_confirm.intro: Review the shape of the instance, then close setup. From this point the wizard is finished: the constants and the game mode lock, and the world opens.
